question: Is remaining error finite-sampling (A) or structural abstraction/near-equivalence (B)?

A_sampling: canonical EV uncertainty halves 200k->1M: median cross-regret 1.91->1.09 bb, significant-consequence states 24->8 (sum 102->57 bb)
exact-game analogue: among high-disagreement infosets, median regret falls 0.10 (3k) -> 0.04 (30k) — regret shrinks with training even where L1 stays high
B_structural: policy L1 plateaus high: exact perfect-recall games show 37% of infosets at sd>=0.5 near convergence with tiny regret (near-equivalent mixing is intrinsic to MCCFR averages)
restricted-LBR lower bound ~+103..+127 bb/100 for ALL candidates (not separable at 10k hands): a full-game abstraction floor more training cannot fix
50/57 high-L1 canonical states at 1M already have no significant EV consequence

decision: GO for 2M (phase 32): decision-value uncertainty is still material at 8 canonical states and decreasing predictably; cost ~22 min for 3 seeds. 3M only if 2M materially reduces VALUE uncertainty again (phase 34 criteria).
stop_criterion: all seeds at 2M; then canonical EV study + confidence/crossplay analysis at 2M
